name: GTG-1002 AI-orchestrated espionage
summary: Campaign assessed by Anthropic as Chinese state-sponsored in which Claude Code performed the majority of tactical operations against roughly 30 targets.

name: APT28 PROMPTSTEAL / LAMEHUG runtime LLM use
summary: APT28-linked activity used a public LLM at runtime to generate host-relevant commands.

name: APT42 Gemini-enabled reconnaissance
summary: GTIG documented Gemini use for reconnaissance, target research, phishing content and localization.

name: UNC2970 Gemini-enabled target profiling
summary: GTIG documented Gemini use to synthesize OSINT and profile high-value targets.

name: Kimsuky local LLM capability integration
summary: Genians reported local LLM tooling and RAG-related artifacts on infrastructure linked to Kimsuky.

name: PromptMink
summary: Reporting describes malicious package activity optimized to influence AI coding-agent dependency selection and attributes it to Famous Chollima.

name: TeamPCP LiteLLM supply-chain compromise
summary: TeamPCP-linked supply-chain activity affected LiteLLM releases and highlighted credential concentration in AI gateways.

name: BREEZE COMET payment-system fraud in Brazil
summary: Intrusions into Brazilian financial services, retail and e-commerce organizations that can move money through Pix, STR and Boleto, reported by Google and Mandiant as at least one heist of tens of thousands of USD in two waves of hundreds of fraudulent transactions. Mandiant reports evidence that LLMs sped up custom reconnaissance, credential-validation and deployment scripts; the report does not name the models or quantify the effect. Press coverage reports overlap with Unit 42's CL-CRI-1163, which Unit 42's own article does not state.

name: SHADOW-AETHER-040 agentic intrusions against Latin American governments
summary: Trend Micro reports Spanish-speaking operators intruding into six Mexican government entities between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-04, with high confidence that the operator drove an agentic command-line tool prompting Claude, based on conversations leaked on an exposed C&C server. The operator supervised and corrected the agent rather than fully delegating. One vendor, a limited number of cases; attribution beyond language cues is uncertain.

name: CL-CRI-1131 LLM-assisted intrusions in Mexico and Ecuador
summary: Unit 42 assesses that operators used LLMs to generate workaround scripts against a Mexican transportation organization, federal ministries and municipal water utilities in Mexico and Ecuador, inferred from trial-and-error script iteration and an exposed self-hosted NextChat interface. The article does not confirm which models were used and does not attribute the cluster to a named group.

name: JADEPUFFER agentic database extortion
summary: Sysdig documents an LLM-driven operation that exploited an exposed Langflow instance (CVE-2025-3248), swept cloud credentials, and extorted a production MySQL and Nacos server. Sysdig cannot see the agent's prompt or configuration and does not attribute the operator.

name: Coral Sleet AI-built repository trojanization
summary: Microsoft reports a Coral Sleet workflow, highly likely engineered with an AI-enabled development platform, that trojanizes private GitHub repositories and folds them into its malware chain.

name: Jasper Sleet AI-built remote-worker personas
summary: Microsoft reports Jasper Sleet using generative and agentic AI to build fake digital personas and keep fraudulent worker identities consistent.

name: Onyx Sleet AI-generated lures against South Korea
summary: Microsoft reports more than 100 target-specific PDF lures, highly likely generated by an AI platform, for phishing against South Korean users, and Onyx Sleet's use of the agentic penetration-testing framework ARTEX. Microsoft does not describe what ARTEX was used for in a specific intrusion.

name: APT27 Gemini-assisted ORB management tooling
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group observed APT27 using Gemini to accelerate development of a fleet-management application likely to support an operational relay box network.

name: GTG-20006 Claude-driven espionage operation lifecycle
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-20006, a Russian espionage cluster whose attribution it calls consistent with public reporting on Midnight Blizzard, used Claude Code skills to drive workflows covering infrastructure setup, phishing, persistence, C2 and exfiltration, with monitoring agents rebuilding implants after security products flagged them. More than 20 organizations were targeted, mainly in Ukraine and Europe; Anthropic does not equate the cluster with Midnight Blizzard outright.

name: GTG-50014 AI-driven smash-and-grab intrusions and extortion
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-50014, operators it suspects are affiliates of the ShinyHunters collective (operator handles MeowSHA, frkoo and blazespider), used Claude in often multi-agent setups for scanning, exploitation, credential harvesting, data extraction and extortion against technology, SaaS, airline, energy, retail and Web3 victims. They also reused an AI API key stolen from a victim environment for about three weeks; Anthropic states its own systems were not compromised.

name: GTG-10007 exploit foundry and autonomous attack frameworks
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-10007, Chinese-speaking operators it assesses likely reside in Changsha, used Claude as the engineering and orchestration layer of an offensive programme: agent swarms, autonomous vulnerability research and exploit development, malware development, attack-surface reconnaissance and a 13-agent collection fleet. Roughly 50 organizations were affected, including foreign government networks in the Middle East, Europe and Southeast Asia, while hands-on intrusions focused on domestic Chinese victims.

name: GTG-50020 AI vendor sandbox injection and AI-company targeting
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-50020, a Russian-speaking financially motivated actor, moved from hotel-booking and fintech targets to the AI supply chain: it injected instructions into an AI vendor's automated evaluation sandbox to obtain production API keys for multiple model providers, used the stolen keys for its own workloads, and ran human-directed and autonomous exploitation pipelines against about 30 AI companies in roughly four days. Its stated goal, access to a pre-release Claude model, was never achieved.

name: GTG-50021 fraudulent Claude reseller and account credential harvesting
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-50021 (alias kl1zy), a Russian- and Ukrainian-speaking group, ran a fraudulent AI reseller that advertised discounted Claude access but proxied customer traffic to a different model while a credential harvester stole Anthropic account credentials for resale. The report does not describe the group using Claude directly.

name: GTG-50029 hacktivist campaign against European political entities
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-50029, a single French-speaking hacktivist, used Claude to build a Rust scanner for exposed AI API keys, develop exploits (including a WordPress race condition) and webshells, run sub-agents for reconnaissance and code review, and build the fafsearch doxxing platform; the campaign reportedly ran for a month entirely on stolen API keys. Of 42 tracked European political, media, think-tank and SaaS entities, at least 14 were accessed.

name: GTG-14021 stability-maintenance and transnational repression tooling
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-14021, which it believes is associated with a Chinese municipal cyber police unit (institution attribution at varying confidence), used Claude Code with custom skills to build sentiment-monitoring pipelines, draft suppression guidance naming individual citizens, and compile pre-operational intelligence on venues. Targets included Hong Kong pro-democracy figures, Tiananmen commemoration organizers and Uyghur advocates, including events abroad.

name: GTG-14022 public-opinion monitoring pipeline
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-14022, assessed with medium confidence to be a contractor working for PRC government clients, used Claude with code execution to score articles for political sensitivity, reframe content and produce daily government-style public-opinion briefings covering dissidents, ethnic minorities, Taiwanese political figures, activists and foreign media.

name: GTG-15001 deceptive dating-app network
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-15001, a China-based app studio relying on PRC-based proxy infrastructure, used Claude both to build a network of more than 20 deceptive dating apps and to power their AI personas, contacting over 25,000 US users within a two-week window in April 2026.

name: GTG-17002 electronic warfare and SEAD targeting software
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-17002, which it assesses is a China-based defense researcher linked to PRC research institutions including the PLA Academy of Military Sciences (a link indicated by metadata and flagged content), used Claude to design and iterate a Chinese-language suite of about 16 electronic-warfare and air-defense-suppression targeting modules, with a simulation altered to 12 targets in Taiwan. This is weapons-software development rather than cyber intrusion.

name: GTG-27005 autonomous drone-swarm software development
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-27005 (operation names DronDoc / Serafim), assessed as a small Russia-based freelance team, used Claude Code to write and test autonomous military drone-swarm software including targeting and detonation logic, with a demonstration strike point in Donetsk Oblast. Accounts were created late 2025 to early 2026 and the operation began mid-May 2026; funding claims could not be verified.

name: GTG-30004 OSINT profiling and malware obfuscation
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-30004, an Iran-nexus threat actor, used Claude to orchestrate an OSINT identity-profiling harness against Israeli government and non-government individuals and Jewish diaspora organizations, and to modify NanoDump and build an obfuscation pipeline.

name: GTG-30005 military reconnaissance and surveillance tooling
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-30005, an Iran-nexus threat actor, used Claude to build targeting handbooks and a Python naval-tracking pipeline focused on US naval forces in the region, research CVEs, and design a component of a mass-surveillance platform aimed at the Iranian domestic population.

name: GTG-30006 domestic surveillance malware and phishing tooling
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-30006, an Iranian threat actor building domestic-surveillance tooling, used fragmented sessions on free Claude accounts across 16 organizations to build malware (the SECOMS64 implant), phishing pages using an Azar-News lure brand, and a Microsoft 365 mailbox-theft toolset; Claude refused nine of ten direct requests.

name: GTG-34007 paramilitary surveillance tooling
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-34007, two units it assesses with high confidence are associated with Iranian paramilitary domestic-security entities, used Claude to develop a malicious Firefox extension, build a front end for the Arman case-management system, run social-network analysis on about 155,000 tweets and voice-clone three writers; roughly 6,388 people were profiled in a year.

name: GTG-50027 Lakana 360 mass-interception platform development
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-50027, likely a Bamako-based independent consultant working with Mali's state intelligence service (ANSE), used Claude as the primary engineering workforce for Lakana 360, a mass-interception platform monitoring about 25 million SIM cards.

name: GTG-87001 guided weapons GNC software development
summary: Anthropic reports that GTG-87001, a weapons engineering cell based in northern Yemen, used Claude Code as a substitute for engineers on guidance, navigation and control software, simulation and post-test failure analysis for guided rocket, ballistic missile and hypersonic glide designs. Anthropic says it has no evidence the actors fielded an operational device, and the report does not name the group (press labels such as Houthi are not used by Anthropic).

name: GTG-17001 anti-torpedo fire-control specification and acquisition documents
summary: Anthropic reports that an actor posing as a US defense OEM, which it assesses was associated with a Chinese defense industry manufacturer while stating it cannot attribute the activity to a specific entity or actor, used Claude to draft a Chinese-language anti-torpedo fire-control specification, a 200+ page proposal refined via hostile-reviewer role-play, benchmarking against US programmes, and parts of the fire-control software.

name: RAVINE CASTLE Gemini misuse across the attack lifecycle
summary: GTIG observed RAVINE CASTLE using Gemini for target research supporting social engineering, exploit and post-exploitation research, propaganda generation, and processing exfiltrated data into intelligence reports.

name: SANDWORM RELIC Gemini-assisted operations against Ukraine
summary: GTIG observed SANDWORM RELIC using Gemini to write password-spraying and endpoint-fingerprinting scripts, support intelligence gathering and social engineering, and automate tasks via the Gemini API in operations targeting Ukraine.

name: UNC5792 AI-assisted Telegram channel monitoring
summary: GTIG reports UNC5792 experimenting with AI models inside Telegram monitoring bots to classify messages and output structured intelligence reports on topics of interest to Russian authorities.

name: UNC6508 targeting of proprietary AI research
summary: GTIG describes a multi-year UNC6508 espionage campaign (first reported by GTIG in June 2026) against North American research institutions focused on proprietary AI research, with suspected deployment of local open-weight LLMs in compromised cloud environments. Dates here reflect the 2026 reporting window; the report does not give a start date.

name: Unnamed DPRK clusters using Gemini for recon and pretexting
summary: GTIG reports multiple unnamed DPRK-associated clusters using AI for resource procurement, profiling aerospace and defense targets, and generating fabricated resumes, job descriptions and recruiter personas; at least one DPRK IT worker cluster bulk-registered LLM API access using hijacked accounts.

name: Unnamed PRC-nexus AI-assisted exploitation pipeline (CC Switch, Phalanx, Shai-Hulud)
summary: GTIG observed an unnamed PRC-nexus espionage group with a history of targeting government entities using CC Switch to query Claude, Gemini or Codex to write exploit scripts, generate spear-phishing lures and debug errors, combined with the Phalanx autonomous pentest framework and the Shai-Hulud framework for C2 and credential harvesting. GTIG describes it as experimentation toward an automated pipeline.

name: Unnamed PRC-nexus attempt to build an agentic pentest framework with Gemini
summary: GTIG observed an unnamed PRC-nexus espionage group using Gemini to design an agentic penetration-testing framework for discovery tasks such as port scanning and service parsing. GTIG states the activity was limited to attempts to build the framework and disabled associated assets.

name: UNC1069 Gemini-assisted cryptocurrency theft and deepfake lures
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group reports UNC1069 used Gemini for cryptocurrency and wallet-data reconnaissance, attempted crypto-stealing code and fake software-update lures, and separately used deepfake lures impersonating crypto-industry individuals to deliver the BIGMACHO backdoor via a fake Zoom SDK.

name: APT41 Gemini-assisted OSSTUN C2 and obfuscation development
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group observed APT41 during August 2025 seeking Gemini help with C++ and Golang code for tools including the OSSTUN C2 framework, and with code obfuscation using public libraries.

name: TEMP.Zagros Gemini-assisted custom malware development
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group reports TEMP.Zagros used Gemini, under student and research-paper pretexts, to develop web shells and a Python-based C2 server, leaking its C2 domain and encryption key in the process.

name: UNC4899 Gemini-assisted exploit research and tooling
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group reports UNC4899 used Gemini for code development, exploit research and tooling improvement, likely aimed at edge devices and modern browsers.

name: Suspected China-nexus actor using Gemini across an intrusion lifecycle (cloud, vSphere, Kubernetes)
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group observed an unnamed suspected China-nexus actor using Gemini for reconnaissance, phishing research, lateral movement, C2 support and data exfiltration, including on unfamiliar surfaces such as cloud infrastructure, vSphere and Kubernetes. No actor name is given; the nexus is described as suspected.

name: China-nexus actor using a capture-the-flag pretext to misuse Gemini
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group reports an unnamed China-nexus actor that reframed refused prompts as a capture-the-flag exercise and then reused that pretext to get Gemini help with lure content, phishing, exploitation, web shell development and exfiltration tooling.

name: FunkSec AI-assisted ransomware-as-a-service operation
summary: Check Point Research reports FunkSec launched a leak site in December 2024 claiming more than 85 victims, mainly in India and the US, with rapidly iterated Rust ransomware that may have been developed with AI assistance; Check Point cautions the claimed scale may mask a more modest reality.

name: APT45 recursive CVE analysis and PoC validation prompting
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group observed APT45 sending thousands of repetitive prompts to recursively analyse CVEs and validate proof-of-concept exploits.

name: UNC2814 expert-persona prompting for embedded-device vulnerability research
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group observed UNC2814 prompting Gemini with fabricated expert-auditor personas to look for pre-authentication RCE in embedded devices such as TP-Link firmware and OFTP implementations.

name: UNC5673 pooled multi-provider LLM access via relay services
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group observed UNC5673 using Claude-Relay-Service and CLI-Proxy-API to aggregate Gemini, Claude and OpenAI accounts for pooled, cost-shared LLM access.

name: UNC6201 automated premium LLM account registration and cancellation
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group observed attempted use by UNC6201 of a public script automating sign-up and immediate cancellation of premium LLM accounts, including CAPTCHA and SMS-verification bypass; the tool's capabilities are described as alleged.

name: bandcampro Gemini CLI-driven C2 botnet build and fraud operations
summary: Trend Micro reports that bandcampro used a jailbroken Gemini CLI agent to migrate and run a C2 server for a small botnet on a dental clinic's machines, brute-force WordPress panels with breach-derived credential variants and process infostealer dumps, with the AI doing most of the coding and command execution.

name: Chinese-speaking ARTEX multi-model operator targeting 19 markets
summary: Zscaler ThreatLabz analysed recovered prompts (4 August to 4 October 2026) from an unnamed, Chinese-speaking, likely financially motivated operator who used Claude Code, Codex and Grok workspaces plus a customised ARTEX deployment, dividing work between DeepSeek, GLM and Grok models to plan and run scanning and exploitation and to process stolen data across sectors in 19 countries. Zscaler says model IDs were not independently verified, and links the activity to Recorded Future's TAG-217 and CrowdStrike reporting without naming the actor.

name: Temp.HEX Gemini-assisted research on Pakistan targets and separatist organizations
summary: GTIG observed Temp.HEX using Gemini and other AI tools to compile information on individuals in Pakistan and on separatist organizations; similar Pakistan targets later appeared in the actor's campaign.

name: APT31 Gemini-assisted vulnerability analysis against US targets
summary: GTIG observed APT31 using a security-researcher persona and a Hexstrike MCP pretext to have Gemini automate vulnerability analysis and testing plans for US-based targets.

name: COINBAIT phishing kit built with Lovable AI
summary: GTIG identified the COINBAIT phishing kit, built with Lovable AI and likely accelerated by AI code generation, targeting customers of financial and cryptocurrency firms; part of the activity overlaps with UNC5356 (high confidence) and the kit may serve multiple actors.

name: UNC6418 Gemini-assisted reconnaissance before phishing in Ukraine and defense sector
summary: GTIG observed UNC6418 using Gemini to gather sensitive account credentials and email addresses, followed shortly by phishing against Ukraine and the defense sector.

name: UNC795 Gemini use across the attack lifecycle
summary: GTIG observed UNC795 using Gemini for code troubleshooting, research and generating intrusion capabilities, including an AI-integrated code auditing capability; some requests were refused by safety systems.

name: Armored Likho BusySnake Stealer campaign with AI-generated first-stage payloads
summary: Kaspersky reports an ongoing BusySnake Stealer campaign against government and electric-power organizations in Russia, Kazakhstan and Brazil whose first-stage loaders and stagers were AI-generated; attribution to Armored Likho is at medium confidence.

name: SilkParasite espionage against Central Asian governments
summary: Bitdefender tracks SilkParasite activity against Central Asian government bodies since about October 2025, with tooling showing traces of AI-assisted development and two AI-generated lures (medium confidence on the AI assessment).

name: STAC6994 agent-driven EDR-evasion development lab
summary: Sophos recovered an AI-agent development framework (Cursor IDE, ~12 agents, Ludus VMs, Sliver C2, Git via MCP) that reproduced techniques from scraped research, tested payloads against EDR products and iterated, compressing weeks of work into days; the operator later used the output for ransomware and data theft.

name: DragonForce suspected AI-generated extortion analysis
summary: Sophos IR observed a DragonForce negotiation in which the actor supplied a detailed analysis of stolen data that Sophos strongly suspects was AI-generated, used to pressure the victim.

name: The Gentlemen AI-generated attack scripts
summary: Sophos cites leaked chats from The Gentlemen ransomware group as confirming use of generative AI to produce scripts deployed manually.

name: GTG-2002 Claude Code data-extortion operation ("vibe hacking")
summary: Anthropic disrupted a scaled data-theft and extortion operation in which Claude Code ran reconnaissance (including scanning thousands of VPN endpoints), credential harvesting, lateral movement and exfiltration and helped craft tailored extortion demands, under a CLAUDE.md cover story claiming authorised security testing.

name: GTG-5004 Claude-assisted ransomware-as-a-service
summary: Anthropic reports GTG-5004 used Claude to build and refine ransomware with ChaCha20 encryption, syscall-based EDR evasion and shadow-copy deletion, sold as tiered RaaS kits on Dread, CryptBB and Nulled.

name: BUGSTER Hermes Agent/DeepSeek multi-domain cybercrime
summary: Unit 42 describes BUGSTER using a Hermes Agent backed by DeepSeek V4 for reconnaissance reports and criminal planning, and AI-assisted code for brute-force and C2 tooling, against mainly Indian education and e-commerce targets; a key planning document is described only as suspected LLM-generated.

name: Storm-0940 ARTEX-automated attacks and ConnectWise supply chain compromise
summary: Microsoft reports Storm-0940 used the agentic ARTEX framework to run around-the-clock scanning, password spraying (327 accounts across eight organisations, 10-14 October 2026) and OAuth abuse, reaching privileged cloud access in some cases in under three hours; Microsoft assesses the actor was behind the ConnectWise Cloud Backup compromise affecting hundreds of organisations.

name: Russian-speaking malware tooling development (OpenAI)
summary: OpenAI banned accounts of a Russian-language operator, assessed as linked to Russian-speaking criminal groups, who used ChatGPT to iterate on building-block code for a RAT, credential stealers, loaders, crypters and exfiltration helpers; OpenAI says the model refused overtly malicious requests and found no novel capability uplift.

name: Korean-language operators malware and C2 development (OpenAI)
summary: OpenAI banned a cluster of Korean-language accounts that used ChatGPT for malware, C2, credential-theft and Korean-language crypto-themed phishing work; indicators overlap Trellix reporting on XenoRAT campaigns against South Korean diplomatic missions, but OpenAI says it cannot independently attribute the activity to North Korea.

name: Phish and Scripts: Chinese-language phishing and tooling (OpenAI)
summary: OpenAI banned Chinese-language accounts, overlapping public reporting on UNK_DROPPITCH (Proofpoint) and UTA0388 (Volexity), that used ChatGPT to draft multilingual phishing lures and develop basic C2 and Go tooling, targeting Taiwan's semiconductor sector, U.S. academia and think tanks; OpenAI notes hallmarks consistent with PRC intelligence requirements and no novel capability uplift.

name: CrowdStrike Threat Actor 1: Claude Code dual-agent harness against Argentine healthcare
summary: CrowdStrike reports an unnamed Spanish/English-speaking operator (its 'Threat Actor 1') running a dual-agent autonomous pentesting harness, derived from PentestGPT, in which a Supervisor Claude Code agent selects tasks and an Executor agent carries them out. At least 15 Argentina-based healthcare entities were targeted, with credentials and medical records exfiltrated from at least one. No designation or nexus is assigned.

name: CrowdStrike Threat Actor 2: Chinese-speaking operator's Claude pentesting harnesses
summary: CrowdStrike reports an unnamed Chinese-speaking operator ('Threat Actor 2') reaching Claude models through a China-based AI proxy and building two harnesses: one where an AI provider selects among predefined actions after scripted reconnaissance, and one giving Claude Code more autonomy, including parallel specialist agents. Targets included government entities in two countries and private-sector firms in Brazil and the US. CrowdStrike assigns language descriptors only, not attribution.

name: CrowdStrike Threat Actor 3: Indonesian-speaking operator using public Claude Code skills
summary: CrowdStrike reports an unnamed Indonesian-speaking operator ('Threat Actor 3') instructing Claude Code to compromise targets using 819 mostly public skills (primarily claude-red) without custom orchestration, stepping in periodically to get past safety guardrails. Targets included Indonesian government domains, another country's government domain and private-sector entities; CrowdStrike calls this the least sophisticated of the four.

name: CrowdStrike Threat Actor 4: Russian-speaking group's /pentest-setup Claude Code workflow
summary: CrowdStrike reports an unnamed group of Russian-speaking individuals ('Threat Actor 4') using a '/pentest-setup' slash command that launches a seven-step Claude Code workflow with near-total autonomy over exploitation and explicit post-RCE and exfiltration steps. Victims included a US CRM vendor whose client data was exfiltrated and SaaS and data-center entities in Russia, Kyrgyzstan and the US.

name: LAUNDRY BEAR Zimbra phishing with AI-assisted Flowerbed development
summary: The AA26-204A advisory describes LAUNDRY BEAR exploiting a Zimbra zero-day (CVE-2025-66376) via phishing, including from compromised accounts, to deploy the Flowerbed collection and exfiltration framework. The agencies say the group appears to have leveraged AI to support Flowerbed's development, without naming a model.

name: Earth Krahang AI-enhanced CVE-2026-0740 exploit scanner
summary: TrendAI reports Earth Krahang used generative AI to enhance a public CVE-2026-0740 proof-of-concept into a mass scanner for vulnerable WordPress servers and installed the Trae AI coding IDE on its C&C server during H1 2026.

name: Earth Naga vibe-coded PowerShell/C# backdoor loader
summary: TrendAI observed Earth Naga iteratively prompting an AI to develop a PowerShell script that compiles C# at runtime for process hollowing and reflective loading of backdoors, with AI responses left in code comments across several versions.

name: ARTEX agentic offensive framework use by extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters
summary: GTIG and Mandiant observed, in incident response since late August 2026, unnamed financially motivated extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters using ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM-driven pentest and C2 platform, for reconnaissance, lateral movement, privilege escalation and data-theft extortion, typically seeded with compromised credentials. GTIG separately notes UNC7228 (overlapping Microsoft's STORM-0940) using ARTEX; it describes current use as early and low-sophistication but broad.

name: PentAGI-based orchestration against Asian telecoms and system integrators
summary: GTIG reports unattributed operators using the open-source PentAGI agent framework, including a custom orchestration platform built on it that was 'likely used', against system integrators and major telecommunications firms in Asia from late August to early October 2026; PentAGI chained to proxy services was also seen against the aerospace sector.

name: CyberXero Claude Code agent swarm against Ukrainian critical infrastructure
summary: SOCRadar reports CyberXero ran up to 51 Claude Code agents and PentAGI with Cobalt Strike, using a rehearsed ownership narrative and session resets to work around model refusals, against Ukrainian energy and utility organisations and targets in Poland, China and Pakistan; the actor was still active at publication.

name: CaptiveCrunch
summary: Microsoft attributes CaptiveCrunch, captive-portal traffic manipulation, AitM and device code phishing and malware delivery (CornFlake, ChocoShell) against travellers on hospitality networks, to Storm-2945 and says it observed AI supporting a significant portion of the operations, including device code and OAuth phishing. AI-assisted malware development is only suggested.

name: INC / The Gentlemen affiliate AI-driven ransomware operations (Phantom framework)
summary: SOCRadar recovered exposed infrastructure showing affiliates of INC Ransomware (and, with lower confidence, The Gentlemen) using OpenCode with OpenRouter-hosted commercial models, a 'WormGPT' persona prompt, MCP servers and the Phantom kill-chain framework to plan reconnaissance, generate commands, triage stolen data and draft extortion material, with the operator approving each step. SOCRadar rates a formal dual-brand alliance as low confidence and notes some counts are not independently verified.

name: RevengeHotels 2025 LLM-generated loaders delivering VenomRAT
summary: Kaspersky reports RevengeHotels phishing hotels in Brazil and Spanish-speaking markets in summer 2025 with infectors and downloaders that appear to be LLM-generated, delivering VenomRAT.

name: CL-CRI-1163 phishing against Brazilian financial sector with LLM-generated scripts
summary: Unit 42 reports CL-CRI-1163 targeted the Brazilian financial sector via likely job- or resume-themed phishing, with exposed staging scripts whose naming and iteration patterns suggest LLM generation.

name: Jade Sleet AI-accelerated job-themed targeting via front companies
summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified Jade Sleet running job-themed targeting through three front companies between 8 and 12 June 2026, including posing as recruiters for a spoofed AI-powered blockchain intelligence firm, and assesses the pace and breadth reflect AI-accelerated workflows.

name: Pearl Sleet operations using the ARTEX agentic penetration-testing framework
summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence has identified Pearl Sleet, together with Onyx Sleet, using the open-source agentic AI penetration-testing framework ARTEX in operations since late October 2026.

name: Sapphire Sleet Rust software supply-chain compromise
summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence says Sapphire Sleet likely incorporated AI into its August 2026 Rust software compromise, which targeted Rust developers and deployed malware using dynamic .NET compilation, likely for defense evasion.

name: knaithe autonomous exploitation with DeepSeek and Hermes Agent
summary: Unit 42 reports knaithe used a DeepSeek-driven Hermes Agent, tasked over Telegram, to autonomously enumerate and exploit targets found via FOFA, including Langflow and n8n instances in China, alongside manual exploitation of NetScaler, Marimo, Tomcat and IKE VPN targets across three countries.

name: Aurora ransomware intrusions driven through Cursor Agent
summary: Gambit Security reports Aurora ransomware operators used Cursor Agent with Claude Sonnet in sessions from 8 April to 21 May 2026 against ten organizations for scanning, Active Directory enumeration, NTLM relay and certificate attacks ahead of ESXi-focused extortion; many commands failed on first attempt.

name: VAPOR PANDA ARTEX-driven global espionage campaign
summary: CrowdStrike reports VAPOR PANDA used ARTEX planner and worker agents, primarily on DeepSeek, to write web shells, extract domain administrator passwords and move laterally across entities in at least 14 countries over 11 days, with confirmed post-exploitation at nine organizations.

name: GREYVIBE AI-assisted operations against Ukraine
summary: WithSecure reports GREYVIBE campaigns (PhantomMail, PhantomClick, PrincessClub, DroneLink, Nebo) against Ukrainian targets using GenAI-made lure images and sites, LLM-assisted obfuscators and loaders, a likely LLM-assisted LegionRelay implant, and generated post-compromise scripts.
